entry.title: Plage de Palavas-les-Flots
entry.summary: Palavas-les-Flots is a seaside town near Montpellier with a wide sandy beach, a promenade and a lighthouse by the canal. The water is shallow and warm in summer. It is easy to reach by tram and bus from Montpellier.

entry.title: Plage de Granville
entry.summary: Granville is a seaside town in Normandy with a sandy beach below its old town on the cliff. The tide here is among the biggest in Europe, so the beach changes dramatically through the day. The water is cool and swimming is best at high tide.

entry.title: Utah Beach, Normandy
entry.summary: Utah Beach is a wide, flat beach on the east coast of the Cotentin peninsula in Normandy, one of the D-Day landing beaches. The sand stretches far at low tide and memorials and a museum stand behind the dunes. The sea is Atlantic and swimming is possible in calm weather.

entry.title: Plage de la Conche des Baleines, Ile de Re
entry.summary: La Conche des Baleines is a wide sandy beach on the north-west tip of Ile de Re, with dunes and the Phare des Baleines lighthouse nearby. It is exposed to Atlantic waves and best for walking and cycling. Swimming depends on the tide and the sea state.

entry.title: Plage de la Palmyre
entry.summary: La Palmyre is a wide sandy beach on the Atlantic coast of Charente-Maritime, beside the Foret de la Coubre. The sea is Atlantic, so it is cooler than the Mediterranean. The resort has a promenade, a zoo nearby and cycle paths through the pines.

entry.title: Platja de Muro, Mallorca
entry.summary: Platja de Muro is a long white-sand beach on Alcudia Bay in north-east Mallorca, with shallow warm water and pine trees behind the dunes. It is wide, family friendly and has lifeguards. Hotels and restaurants lie behind the beach.

entry.title: Plage du Lotu, Corsica
entry.summary: Lotu is a white-sand beach with turquoise water in the Desert des Agriates on the north coast of Corsica. It has no road, so most visitors arrive by boat from Saint-Florent or on foot along a long track. There are no facilities, so bring water and shade.

entry.title: Platja de Migjorn, Formentera
entry.summary: Platja de Migjorn is a long sandy beach on the south coast of Formentera, running for several kilometres. It is quieter than Ses Illetes, with beach bars spread along the sand. The water is clear but can be rougher with southern winds.

entry.title: Ses Illetes Beach, Formentera
entry.summary: Ses Illetes is a narrow peninsula on the north of Formentera, with white sand and shallow water in a Mediterranean turquoise. The beach is protected as part of a natural park. Beach clubs and a few restaurants sit behind the sand, and parking is limited and paid.

entry.title: Sarti Beach, Sithonia
entry.summary: Sarti is a wide, gently sloping bay on the east coast of Sithonia, with sand and a few pebbles. The view looks across the Singitic Gulf toward Mount Athos. The village has tavernas and cafes behind the beach.

entry.title: Porto Limnionas, Zakynthos
entry.summary: Porto Limnionas is a narrow rocky inlet on the north-west coast of Zakynthos, with clear deep water and no sand. Swimmers enter from flat rocks and ladders, and snorkellers come for the underwater views. A couple of tavernas sit above the water.

entry.title: Manganari Beach, Ios
entry.summary: Manganari is a group of sandy bays on the south coast of Ios, known for turquoise water and fine sand. It is one of the best-known beaches on the island and has tavernas and sunbeds. A road and a boat both reach it from the port.

entry.title: Sougia Beach, Crete
entry.summary: Sougia is a small village on the south-west coast of Crete with a long pebble beach in front of its tavernas. It is quiet, with clear water and an end-of-the-road feel, and the E4 trail starts nearby. The road in winds down from the mountains and the village can also be reached by ferry from Paleochora.

entry.title: Son Bou Beach, Menorca
entry.summary: Son Bou is the longest beach on Menorca, a wide strip of golden sand on the south coast backed by dunes and a hotel strip. The water is clear and gets deep gradually. The ends of the beach are quieter, and a short walk leads to a cliff with caves.

entry.title: Agia Anna Beach, Amorgos
entry.summary: Agia Anna is a small pebble beach on the east coast of Amorgos, directly below the white Chozoviotissa monastery clinging to the cliff. The water is deep blue and clear, and the beach sits in a rocky cove. It is a short drive from Chora and has a small taverna nearby.

entry.title: Praia de Porto Pim, Horta
entry.summary: Porto Pim is a sheltered curved bay on Faial next to Horta, with grey-gold sand, calm water and a view of Monte da Guia. It is good for swimming and snorkelling, and the old whaling museum is nearby. The Horta marina is a short walk away.

entry.title: Praia Formosa, Santa Maria
entry.summary: Praia Formosa is the main sandy beach on Santa Maria, the only Azores island with real golden sand. It is a wide beach with clear water, backed by a lawn and bar, and hosts a well-known music festival in August. The water stays cooler than the mainland.

entry.title: Praia do Vau, Portimao
entry.summary: Praia do Vau is a sandy cove near Portimao in the Algarve, enclosed by golden cliffs and rock stacks. The water is clear and the beach has lifeguards and restaurants behind it. A cliff path leads to neighbouring beaches.

entry.title: Praia da Oura, Albufeira
entry.summary: Praia da Oura is a wide golden beach backed by low cliffs just east of the Albufeira old town. It has beach bars, lifeguards and calm water, and the lively Strip is close. It is busy in July and August but easy to reach.

entry.title: Grama Bay, Karaburun
entry.summary: Grama Bay is a sheltered cove on the Karaburun peninsula, with a pebble beach, clear water and inscriptions carved into the rock by ancient visitors. It is mostly visited by boat from Vlore. There are no facilities on shore.

entry.title: Porto Palermo Beach, Himara
entry.summary: Porto Palermo is a sheltered bay on the Albanian Riviera near Himara, with a pebble beach and a small Ali Pasha castle on the peninsula. The water is clear and calm. A few cafes sit near the bay and the setting is quiet.

entry.title: Shengjin Beach, Lezhe
entry.summary: Shengjin is a small port town on the Adriatic coast of northern Albania with a long sandy beach, a promenade and many cafes and hotels. The water is shallow and warm, which suits families. It is far less crowded than the better-known resorts further south.

entry.title: Anchor Bay, Popeye Village
entry.summary: Anchor Bay is a small pebble and rock bay below Popeye Village on the north-west coast of Malta, framed by cliffs and the colourful film-set village. The water is clear and sheltered. Entry to the village is ticketed and the beach is small.

entry.title: Fond Ghadir, Sliema
entry.summary: Fond Ghadir is a rocky swim spot on the Sliema seafront in Malta, with flat platforms, ladders and clear water beside the promenade. There is no sand. It is very convenient for a quick swim from the city, and there is a lido nearby.

entry.title: Marsalforn Bay, Gozo
entry.summary: Marsalforn is a small town on the north coast of Gozo with a sheltered bay, a small beach of sand and pebbles and a promenade lined with restaurants and cafes. The water is clear and calm in summer. Dive centres operate here and the rocks nearby are good for snorkelling.

entry.title: Qbajjar Bay, Gozo
entry.summary: Qbajjar Bay is a rocky bay on the north coast of Gozo near Marsalforn, next to the old salt pans. Swimming is from the flat rocks into clear water and there are a few restaurants nearby. It is a quiet spot, but there is little sand.

entry.title: Wied il-Ghasri, Gozo
entry.summary: Wied il-Ghasri is a narrow inlet cut into the cliffs on the north-west coast of Gozo, reached by steps down the gorge. A small area of sand and pebbles sits at the bottom and the water is very clear. There are no facilities and the sea can be rough, so it suits calm days.

entry.title: Ghar Lapsi, Siggiewi
entry.summary: Ghar Lapsi is a small rocky inlet on the south-west coast of Malta near Siggiewi, with ladders and flat rock platforms for swimming and no sand. The water is deep and very clear, which makes it a popular spot with divers and snorkellers. A couple of restaurants overlook the inlet.

entry.title: Veliki Pijesak Beach, Ulcinj
entry.summary: Veliki Pijesak is a sandy beach near Ulcinj on the south Montenegrin coast, with shallow warm water that suits families. Beach bars and cafes line the shore in summer. The wider Ulcinj area is known for its long sandy beaches and warm sea.

entry.title: Plavi Horizonti Beach, Lustica
entry.summary: Plavi Horizonti is a wide, clean beach on the Lustica peninsula, with fine pebbles, some sand and very clear water. The sea gets deep gradually. Beach bars and restaurants are set behind the shore and there is parking nearby.
